channel.title: Hong Kong Free Press - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Hong Kong Free Press (hongkongfp.com)

item.title: Revised HK$2 public transport scheme for elderly to begin April 3
item.description: A revised version of the HK$2 scheme, which will require the elderly to pay higher fares for some public transport routes, will take effect on April 3, the government has announced.

item.title: HK upgrades Iran, Israel travel alerts to 'black' amid Mideast war
item.description: HK authorities have raised the travel alert for Iran and Israel to black - the highest level - signifying a “severe threat” amid an ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: Taiwan's opposition leader says talks with Xi a 'bridge' to peace
item.description: The leader of Taiwan's largest opposition party said Monday she hoped to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and build a "bridge" to resolve disputes between China and the democratic island, which Beijing has threatened to seize by force.

item.title: Hong Kong to hike local, international postage rates in mid-April
item.description: Postal rates in Hong Kong are to be increased from April 13, with Hongkong Post citing "increases in major cost components such as conveyance costs and terminal dues payments."

item.title: Claims gov’t ‘tipped off’ consultant over safety checks ‘groundless,’ lawyer says
item.description: Accusations that a Housing Bureau inspection unit “tipped off” a renovation consultant at the fire-hit Wang Fuk Court about safety checks were “groundless” and amounted to “prejudgment,” a lawyer for the government has told a public inquiry.

item.title: New Macau nat. sec law open to government 'misuse': rights group
item.description: A new Macau law that allows judges to hear national security cases behind closed doors and which came into effect on Tuesday could be open to potential misuse by the government, a rights group said.

item.title: HK to see record heat in 2026 as UN raises alarm over climate crisis
item.description: Hong Kong is set to see abnormally high temperatures in 2026, the Observatory has said. It comes after residents saw the hottest winter on record.

item.title: HK proposes blanket smoking ban on construction sites
item.description: The HK government has unveiled its proposal for a blanket smoking ban on construction sites, seeking to impose hefty fines and possible jail time for workers and contractors.

item.title: HK indy bookstore staff arrested; Jimmy Lai book among titles seized - report
item.description: Hong Kong independent bookseller Pong Yat-ming and three of his staff have reportedly been arrested on suspicion of selling seditious titles, including a biography of jailed media tycoon Jimmy Lai.

item.title: 3 Tai Po fire survivors recount escapes amid silent fire alarms
item.description: 3 survivors of the fatal Wang Fuk Court blaze in November have testified at a public inquiry, recalling their narrow escapes from the burning housing estate without hearing any fire alarms.

item.title: Ex-Hong Kong police officer denies spying for China in UK trial
item.description: A retired Hong Kong police superintendent Tuesday denied spying for Beijing, telling a London court he played no part in directing shadow policing operations for China on UK soil.

item.title: 3 Apple Daily firms declared ‘prohibited organisations’ after gov’t deregistration
item.description: 3 companies linked to the now-defunct Apple Daily newspaper have become “prohibited organisations” after the Hong Kong government removed them from the corporate registry.

item.title: HK court dismisses appeal by Swedish businessman convicted of rape
item.description: HK's Court of Appeal has upheld a Swedish businessman's conviction for rape and buggery of his former domestic worker and sent him back to jail.

item.title: Japan calls Chinese embassy break-in 'regrettable'
item.description: Japan said Wednesday it was "regrettable" that a member of the Japanese military broke into the Chinese embassy in Tokyo, after Beijing expressed shock over the incident.

item.title: Tiananmen vigils meant to honour victims, not incite subversion: activist
item.description: A HK activist has said that annual Tiananmen vigils were meant to commemorate those killed in the crackdown, not incite subversion or promote her group’s ideals.
